items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Helvey and a few other members of the orchestra including myself decided to go to Dayton to hear the McKinney orchestra.

ctx.x: Others that I heard in Cincy that had big names where "Speed" Webb and Alfonso Trent and Bellson, an orchestra from West Virginia and [that] Bobby Robinson and John Nesbit had played with.

Helvey took a job across the river in Newport, Ky., at a Road House and a new drummer joined the orchestra. Towles left with a T.O.B.A. show called the Whitman? Westman Sisters. I had seen this show in Cincinnati and I remember that one of the sisters named Alice was a wonderful tap dancer. The new drummer was John Hargrave and he was a better drummer than Towles.
And it was at that time that Madelyn and I got married. I had said when I was younger that I would not get married until I was 35 years old and here I was, getting married at 21.
